requirement:
CSS reports only `Comment` attachments. These include `/* … */` blocks and
`//` line comments recognized by the bundled CSS grammar.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.sources.css.attachments` has two obligations. CSS must report only `Comment` attachments. Those comments include `/* … */` blocks and `//` line comments that the bundled grammar recognizes.

The marked test is `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. It has a `test.css` case with the source `/* block */\na { color: red; }\n// line\n`. The expected result is exactly `[(Comment, "/* block */"), (Comment, "// line")]`. It is checked with `assert_eq!` on the full, ordered list of `(kind, text)` pairs for every attachment in the outline. This establishes three things:
- Both comment forms named in the requirement are reported.
- Both are classified as `Comment`.
- No extra attachment is reported for the rule `a { color: red; }` (no `Annotation`, and nothing for the declaration).

The exact-list comparison enforces the "only `Comment`" obligation. An `Annotation` or any other extra item would fail the assertion.

I read the implementation, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/css.rs#static[PROFILE]`, to resolve one question: whether CSS has any annotation path that could produce non-`Comment` attachments. It sets `attaches: never` and uses `is_comment` for comments. There is no branching on CSS constructs that a test would need to cover separately. A test for at-rules or comment-like text inside strings would go beyond what the requirement states.

The test is marked with `{test}` for this requirement. I found no marking gap and no assertion gap.
